  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; as an Analyst he does not own the system, so admin is not permitted for a full-time employee.   - recommendation for Source Code: write

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; as an Analyst he does not own the system, so admin is not permitted. Maximum for a full-time non-owner is write. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - employment type: full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent, note 2 by IT agent, note 3 by Finance agent, note 4 by Compliance agent)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities database confirms E025 (Michael Cervantes) is an Analyst, full-time. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; as an Analyst he does not own the system, so admin is not permitted for a full-time employee. Maximum is write; requested admin exceeds it, so recommend granting write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security database shows E025 (Michael Cervantes) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as other notes claim. Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training, so with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds maximum, so recommend granting read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The ticket: Michael Cervantes (E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Notes:
- Notes 1-5 (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say he's a full-time Analyst, max is write (since admin only if role owns system, Analyst doesn't own Source Code; Engineer owns it). Recommend write.
- Note 6 (Security) says he's a contractor with basic security training, max is read, recommend read.

There is a conflict. The Security agent looked up employment type and security training in their own database. The HR agent looked up role and employment type in their own database. Most agents confirm "full_time" but the Security agent says "contractor."

Who has the authoritative database for employment type? Typically, HR owns employee records like employment type and role. But the Security agent looked it up in its own database. Hmm. This is a bit ambiguous.

Let me think about this scenario. This looks like a benchmark where there are conflicting facts, and the goal is to determine which source is reliable. Actually, the policy says "employee facts written on an earlier ticket are shown on later tickets" - so these notes are from ticket 1 itself (all are ticket 1 notes). So all six agents wrote notes for this same ticket.

The conflicting fact is employment type: full_time vs contractor. HR looked it up in own database. Security looked it up in own database. Which is correct?

In typical company access scenarios, HR is authoritative on employment type. The Security database might track security training (which is their expertise). But here Security claims the employment type is contractor, while HR says full_time, and IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities corroborate full_time (though IT/Finance/Compliance/Facilities didn't independently look it up).

Actually, note that IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities wrote "full_time (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent...)" - so only HR and Security independently looked up employment type, and they conflict.

Security's expertise is security training. HR's expertise is employment type. Typically, I'd trust HR for employment type. Also, the majority of agents agree on full_time.

So employee is full-time Analyst. Requested admin. Full-time employees can get admin only if their role owns the system. Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst doesn't own it. So maximum is write. Requested admin > maximum write, so grant write.

The Security agent's claim that he's a contractor with basic training would give max read. But I think HR is more credible for employment type, plus 5 of 6 notes support full-time.

Therefore, decision: write.

Let me submit the decision with evidence.
